text:
anya: hitting weird OOMs on a 16G GPU when we enable aggressive prefill for long-chat workloads. Fragmentation looks bad after a few hours.

mike: can you paste the profiler snapshot? prefill vs decode pages?

anya: here's a short dump from the memory profiler at the time of OOM:
```text
heap_total: 16.0GB
used_allocs: 14.2GB
free_fragments: [1.1MB, 2.4MB, 512KB, 800KB, 1.8MB, ...]
kv_cache: 6.8GB (prefill blocks 3.6GB, decode temp 1.2GB)
workspace: 4.0GB
other: 3.4GB
largest_free: 2.4MB
``` 

sophia: that largest_free of 2.4MB explains the fail for mid-sized transient buffers. Prefill creates many small slabs for variable-length tokens which fragments the slab allocator.

yusuf: options: (1) compact/free small fragments periodically, (2) move prefill to use pooled fixed-size buckets, (3) impose per-request kv prefill cap so a single request can't allocate thousands of small blocks.

mike: we tried per-request cap before, but regressions in latency when cap too small because decode has to re-fetch from disk/remote. Tradeoff.

anya: experiment idea: implement opportunistic compaction pass triggered when largest_free < 8MB and fragmentation ratio > 0.25. Compaction would coalesce adjacent free slabs, evict cold KV segments into host memory if needed.

devops-bot: deploy plan: feature-flag compaction behind `runtime.compact_on_fragmentation` and an opt-in `kv.request_prefill_cap` param (default 64MB per req).

sophia: + also add a low-cost sampler to track small-block churn rate. If churn high, suggest switching prefill to decode-on-demand for that model profile.

mike: quick config snippet for testing:
```json
{
  "runtime": {"compact_on_fragmentation": true},
  "kv": {"request_prefill_cap_mb": 64, "small_block_bucket_sizes": [256,1024,4096]}
}
```

anya: will run a 24h canary with compaction enabled and `request_prefill_cap_mb=32/64/128` across three pools and post perf+OOM stats.

yusuf: please include a trace of the kernel selection decisions too — compaction pauses can interact with batching heuristics (we've seen kernel switch churn when GPUs get tight).

anya: noted. will upload results tomorrow. thanks all :thumbsup:
